points: Q2 2026 already showed strong results and improved profitability, so the November Q3 print will test whether that momentum carried through the summer and into the fall freight season.
Reports suggest management guided Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $35M-$45M, with brokerage momentum expected to offset last-mile headwinds; the print will reveal if that mix played out as described.

The 90-day revenue estimate has been revised up 112% and the 30-day analyst revision count is 12 up versus 1 down, so the print will show whether that bullish estimate reset was justified or overdone.
Consensus expects FY1 EPS of $0.12 and FY2 EPS of $0.61, implying roughly 4x earnings growth; the Q3 print and any Q4 commentary will shape whether that FY2 acceleration looks credible.
RXO reports after JBHT, KNX, and ARCB and on the same day as MRTN, so its results will reveal whether the asset-light brokerage model is diverging from asset-heavy truckload peers.
Reports suggest RXO sees an advantage from shifting freight-broker regulations; the print and call commentary will reveal whether scaled brokerage is actually taking share.
The valuation flag shows a P/E premium of 5.1x the theme median but a PEG near 1.0x the theme median, so the long case depends on the consensus 4x EPS growth trajectory remaining intact.
watch: Q3 adjusted EBITDA at or above the $35M-$45M range — supports the long
Revenue growth and upward estimate momentum continuing post-print — supports the long
Brokerage volume/load growth or market-share gains — supports the long
FY2 EPS estimates holding or moving higher rather than being cut — supports the long
